title: Tokyo Opener ‘Sukiyaki’ Director Zeze Takahisa on the Protest Roots of a Global Japanese Pop Hit: ‘The Culture Used to Be Wide Open – Now It’s Become Narrower’
content:
ByMark Schilling

Japan Correspondent

The opening film of the 39thTokyo International Film Festival,Zeze Takahisa’s “Sukiyaki” tells the story of how the title tune became a worldwide hit in 1963 as well as a beloved standard that has been recorded in foreign-language versions that have also topped charts.

The film goes beyond the song itself to delve into the lives and careers of its makers: lyricist Ei Roksuke (Matsuzaka Tori), composer Nakamura Hachidai (Okada Junichi), and singer Sakamoto Kyu (Nakano Taiga). They became known in Japan as the “689 trio” with the unusual moniker coming from the “number” characters in their names: Hachi (8), Roku (6) and Kyu (9). But as the film shows in scene after highly charged dramatic scene, their professional and personal relationships were not always harmonious.

Interviewed at the headquarters of Toho, the film’s Japan distributor, Zeze stressed the film’s relevance, six decades after “Sukiyaki,” known locally as “Ue o Muite Aruko” (I’ll Walk with My Head Up”), first hit the charts. “Back then the country was recovering from the war and all sorts of influences were flooding in from abroad,” Zeze said. “Those influences created an energy that propelled the popular culture here. Now Japan is absorbing fewer influences from abroad. The culture used to be wide open – now it’s become narrower.”

But younger Japanese are now discovering that energy from the Showa Era (1926-1989), the period of Emperor Showa’s reign, when Japanese pop culture was at a fertile peak. Together with nostalgic Boomers, they could be found in the audience of “Godzilla Minus One,” the 2023 smash hit Godzilla series installment set in the early postwar period . The follow-up by director Yamazaki Takashi, “Godzilla Minus Zero” is also at TIFF as the festival’s Centerpiece screening, “It’s a kind of Showa boom,” joked Zeze.

In casting “Sukiyaki,” he says, the main criterion was not a physical resemblance to its main characters, though Nakano Taiga channels Sakamoto’s exuberant stage persona with an uncanny precision. “It was more about the feeling the actors projected,” Zeze explains. “But Taiga comes from a show business family with roots in film’s period so he had a natural affinity for the role. Also, when Sakamoto sings in the film, it’s Taiga’s voice you’re hearing – he has an amazing talent as a vocalist.”

The film’s drama, though, centers more on Nakamura and Ei, who joined forces to compose a series of hits in the 1960s but quarreled and parted as Nakamura spiraled into alcoholism. “ Nakamura went through a tough period after ‘Sukiyaki’ became a hit so we show that,” says Zeze. “If the film were just a success story, it wouldn’t be interesting – it has to have both ups and downs.”

None of this drama had much to do with “Sukiyaki” becoming a hit abroad, but the film also delves into the sources of its creation, from Nakamura’s mastery of the jazz piano, which he displayed in New York clubs, to Sakamoto’s roots into early rock – he was a big Elvis fan – and Ei’s composition of the poignant Japanese lyrics,

“Of course people abroad didn’t understand the lyrics, but the song’s energy came across to them,” says Zeze. “The lyrics reflect what was happening in Japan at that time.” Ei Rokusuke, the lyricist, was inspired by the demonstrations against the Japan-US Security Treaty in 1960. “ The demonstrators called for peace, but failed to stop the treaty ratification. “He wanted them to ‘walk with their heads up,’ despite their defeat,” says Zeze. “So the song has depth – it ‘s not just a cheery pop tune.”
title_zh: 東京開幕片《壽喜燒》(Sukiyaki) 導演是枝貴史(Zeze Takahisa) 談全球日本流行音樂熱潮的抗議根源：「文化曾經是非常開放的——現在變得狹隘了。」
content_zh:
作者：馬克·希林(Mark Schilling)

日本特派員

第39屆東京國際電影節的開幕影片是是枝貴仁(Zeze Takahisa)的《壽喜燒(Sukiyaki)》，講述了這首標題曲在1963年如何成為全球熱門歌曲，以及成為一首被翻唱成多種外語版本並登上音樂排行榜的經典之作。

這部電影不僅僅聚焦於這首歌本身，還深入探討了創作這首歌的製作人們的生活和職業：作詞家六角英(松坂桃李(Matsuzaka Tori))、作曲家中村八大(岡田準一(Okada Junichi))和歌手坂本九(中野大賀(Nakano Taiga))。他們在日本被稱為“689三人組”，這個不尋常的名字源於他們名字中的“數字”字符：八(8)、六(6)和九(9)。但正如電影中一幕幕充滿張力的戲劇場景所展示的，他們的職業和個人關係並不總是和諧的。

在東寶(Toho)的總部接受採訪時，是枝強調了這部電影的相關性，距離《壽喜燒》在1963年首次登上排行榜已經過去了六十年，這首歌在當地被稱為《仰望天空走(Ue o Muite Aruko)》。他說：“那時候國家正在從戰爭中恢復，各種外來影響源源不斷地湧入。”他補充道：“這些影響創造了一種能量，推動了這裡的流行文化。現在日本從外部吸收的影響變少了。文化曾經是非常開放的——現在變得狹隘了。”

不過，年輕的日本人現在正在重新發現昭和時代(1926-1989)的那種能量，這是一個日本流行文化繁榮的高峰期。與懷舊的嬰兒潮一代一起，他們可以在2023年大熱的《哥吉拉：零號(Godzilla Minus One)》的觀眾中找到身影，這部電影設定在戰後早期。導演山崎貴(Yamazaki Takashi)的後續作品《哥吉拉：零(Godzilla Minus Zero)》也在東京電影節作為中心放映，“這是一種昭和的繁榮，”是枝開玩笑道。

在選角《壽喜燒》時，他表示，主要標準並不是與主要角色的外貌相似，儘管中野大賀的表現完美地捕捉了坂本的活力舞台形象。“更重要的是演員所傳達的感覺，”是枝解釋道。“但大賀來自一個與電影時代有根基的演藝世家，因此他對這個角色有著自然的親和力。此外，當坂本在電影中唱歌時，聽到的正是大賀的聲音——他是一位非常出色的歌手。”

不過，這部電影的戲劇性更多地集中在中村和英身上，他們在1960年代聯手創作了一系列熱門歌曲，但隨著中村陷入酗酒，兩人發生了爭吵並分道揚鑣。“中村在《壽喜燒》成為熱門歌曲後經歷了一段艱難的時期，因此我們展示了這一點，”是枝說。“如果這部電影只是成功的故事，那就不有趣了——它必須有起伏。”

這些戲劇性事件與《壽喜燒(Sukiyaki)》在國外成為熱門歌曲並沒有太大關聯，但這部電影也深入探討了其創作的來源，從中村八大(Nakamura Masao)在紐約俱樂部展示的爵士鋼琴技藝，到坂本九(Sakamoto Kyu)對早期搖滾的根源——他是個大艾維斯·普雷斯利(Elvis Presley)粉絲——以及Ei Rokusuke的感人日文歌詞創作。

Zeze表示：「當然，國外的人們並不理解歌詞，但歌曲的能量卻能傳達給他們。」他補充道：「這些歌詞反映了當時日本發生的事情。」作詞者Ei Rokusuke受到1960年反對日美安保條約示威活動的啟發。「示威者呼籲和平，但未能阻止條約的批准。」Zeze說：「他希望他們在失敗中仍能‘昂首闊步’。」因此，這首歌具有深度——它不僅僅是一首快樂的流行曲。
